original_question: Is the additivity number add(U_fin(Γ, O)) equal to b?
target_in_paper: Section 8.3 (Unions), Problem 10: whether add(Ufin(Γ, O)) equals b.
correct_elements: Your draft already pinpoints the exact open problem stated in the paper: it uses the correct property Ufin(Γ, O), the correct invariant add(·), and the correct comparison cardinal b, and it asks the right equality question.
missing_details: The paper’s default ambient scope is sets of reals (unless stated otherwise), not arbitrary topological spaces.
Γ must be unpacked as the family of open γ-covers of X, where a cover is nontrivial and a γ-cover is infinite with each x in X belonging to all but finitely many members.
O must be unpacked as the family of open covers of X.
Ufin(Γ, O) must be defined explicitly: for every sequence of members of Γ with no finite subcover, one chooses finite subfamilies whose unions form an open cover.
add(Ufin(Γ, O)) should be spelled out as the least cardinal κ such that some union of κ sets of reals, each satisfying Ufin(Γ, O), fails to satisfy Ufin(Γ, O).
b should be defined as the least cardinality of an unbounded subset of ℕ^ℕ under eventual domination ≤*.
If full paper-faithful context is desired, the known bounds b ≤ add(Ufin(Γ, O)) ≤ cf(d) should be mentioned, since the paper records them right next to Problem 10.
refined_question: For the class of sets of reals X, let O be the family of nontrivial open covers of X and Γ the family of open γ-covers of X, where a γ-cover is an infinite open cover such that each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members. Let Ufin(Γ, O) denote the property that for every sequence ⟨Un : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of members of Γ with no finite subcover, there exist finite subfamilies Fn ⊆ Un such that {⋃Fn : n ∈ ℕ} is an open cover of X. If add(Ufin(Γ, O)) is the least cardinal κ such that there exist sets of reals {Xα : α < κ}, each satisfying Ufin(Γ, O), whose union fails Ufin(Γ, O), is add(Ufin(Γ, O)) equal to b, the least cardinality of an unbounded family in (ℕ^ℕ, ≤*)?
justification: This is exactly the question posed as Problem 10 in §8.3. The draft is already very close to the paper’s wording, but it is not stand-alone because the notation is imported from earlier sections: §2.1 defines Ufin(U, V), §2.3 fixes the default setting to sets of reals, §3 defines nontrivial covers, γ-covers, and the families O and Γ, and §6 defines b. The nearby context in §8.3 also records the sharp bounds b ≤ add(Ufin(Γ, O)) ≤ cf(d). Later, §10 recalls the equivalence Ufin(Γ, O) ⇔ Sfin(Ω, O), which helps confirm the intended selection principle. The notes added in proof report that the eventual answer to Problem 10 is negative, but the target question in the body of the paper is exactly the one refined above.
